title: Wrong Number
synopsis: A voice on the line says, 'You weren't supposed to pick up.'

nodes.text: Unknown number. 11:47 p.m. Voice will follow either decision, but it will meet a different version of you after “Answer” than after “Decline.”

choices.consequence: You answer. The way toward Voice opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.
You decline. The way toward Voice opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: Calm, female, careful. She asks if you can keep a secret. Both choices lead to Address, but “Yes” arrives there with a different cost than “Hang up.”

choices.consequence: You choose to yes. By Address, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.
You hang up. The way toward Address opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: She gives you an address. A bus station. Locker 47. You cannot avoid Locker; you can only decide whether “Write it down” or “Repeat it back skeptically” defines the person who reaches it.

choices.consequence: You write it down. The way toward Locker opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.
You repeat it back skeptically. The way toward Locker opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: You go in the morning. There's a phone in the locker. It rings. She Explains will follow either decision, but it will meet a different version of you after “Pick up” than after “Walk away.”

choices.consequence: You commit to pick up. It carries you into She Explains while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.
You commit to walk away. It carries you into She Explains while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: She is in danger. She needs you to mail an envelope. The road still runs toward Done. Its next turn depends on the difference between choosing “Mail it” and choosing “Open it first.”

choices.consequence: You mail it. The way toward Done opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.
You open it first. The way toward Done opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: You drop it in the box. A week later, a news story. A man indicted. To choose “Note the story” means meeting Anonymous Donor; “Don't note” sends you toward Coffee, Months Later instead.

choices.consequence: You commit to note the story. It carries you into Anonymous Donor while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.
You choose to don't note. By Coffee, Months Later, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: Your envelope was, the story implies, the key piece. Nobody ever knows it was you. The road into Anonymous Donor began with “Note the story” in Done; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.
She finds you. She buys you coffee. She does not, you notice, tell you her real name. You don't mind.
